reason: E1 supports that semi-coherent boundaries reduce pile-ups in the BCC phase and promote work hardening in the FCC phase, but does not directly show that pile-ups at these boundaries cause brittle failure. E2 directly demonstrates that phase-selective recrystallization in a eutectic HEA achieves ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress, fully supporting the core premises of the intervention, mechanism, and predicted outcome. The representation of E1 is slightly overstated regarding the direct cause of brittleness, but the overall key premises are strongly supported by E2.
premises: Dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent phase boundaries in eutectic HEAs cause stress concentration and brittle failure
Phase-selective recrystallization can selectively recrystallize the soft FCC phase while preserving the hard phase
Recrystallizing the FCC phase reduces dislocation density and pile-ups at internal boundaries
Preserving strong semi-coherent boundaries maintains or improves work hardening and strength
This treatment can achieve ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress in a eutectic HEA
